rules.claim: The GET collaborators/{collaborator}/permission route enters GetRepoPermissions.
The endpoint route enters GetRepoPermissions for GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{collaborator}/permission.
The target identity is taken from the collaborator path parameter.
The request is rejected when the doer is not an admin, the collaborator path name does not case-insensitively equal the doer's LowerName, and the doer is not a repository admin.
A non-admin, non-repository-admin caller querying a different collaborator name is denied with HTTP 403 before target-user lookup or permission calculation.
If any of the three authorization alternatives holds—global admin, case-insensitive self-name match, or repository admin—the handler continues to look up the named collaborator.
After successful target lookup and repository-permission calculation, the handler returns HTTP 200 JSON containing the named collaborator and permission.AccessMode via convert.ToUserAndPermission.

rules.claim: The handler binds collaboratorUsername from the collaborator path parameter.

The handler allows continuation when the doer is an instance administrator, the doer's lower-case name equals the requested collaborator username case-insensitively, or the doer is a repository administrator; otherwise it rejects.
If none of the administrator, case-insensitive self-name, or repository-administrator conditions holds, the handler returns HTTP 403 and stops before user lookup and permission calculation.
If an administrator, case-insensitive self-name, or repository-administrator condition holds, the handler continues to target-user lookup.
After successful lookup and permission calculation, the handler returns HTTP 200 JSON containing the target user and the calculated repository access mode.
